div.head: Af 31.1
div.ab: Gif hloð ðis gedó ond eft oþswerian wille, teo (man) hy ealle; ond þonne ealle forgilden ðone wær gemænum hondum ond ealle ón wite, swa to þam were belimpe.
Gif hloð ðis gedó ⁊ eft oðswerian wille, tio hie ealle; ⁊ þonne ealle forgielden þone wer gemænum hondum ⁊ ealle án wite, swa to ðam were belimpe.

Si hloþ (id est cohors uel collectum contubernium) hoc faciat et postea negare uelint, incausentur omnes; et omnes mortis illius compositionem coniectent in commune, et omnes unam witam persoluant, sicut ad ipsam weram pertinebit.
Gif hloð ðis gedó ⁊ eft oðswerian wille, tio hie ealle; ⁊ þonne ealle forgielden þone wer gemænum hondum ⁊ ealle án wite, swa to ðam were belimpe.
If the band should do this, and afterwards wish to deny it, let them all be accused; and then let all pay the wer communally and all a single fine, such as is appropriate to the wer.
If a band of marauders acts thus and afterwards wishes to deny it, thay shall all be accused, and then all collectively shall pay the wergeld and fine—whichever is appropriate to the wergeld.

If a band of men does this and afterwards wishes to deny it on oath, they are all to be accused; and then they are all collectively to pay the wergild, and all one fine, as is accordant to the wergild.

Wenn eine Bande dies verübt, [der Todtschläger] jedoch nachher eidlich ableugnen will, so bezichtige [Kläger] sie alle; und darauf sollen alle mit gemeinsamer Hand das Wergeld [des Erschlagenen ihm] zahlen und alle [dem Richter das] Eine Strafgeld, wie es zu jenem Wergeld gehört.

If a band commits this, but [the slayer] afterwards wishes to deny it on oath, let [the plaintiff] accuse them all; and then let them all pay [him] the wergeld [of the slain] with joint hand and all [pay the judge the] one fine, as belongs to that wergeld.
div.note: i.e. each wishes to deny being the actual slayer.
Whitelock numbers this chapter 31.1 and gives Liebermann’s number, 31.1, in brackets.
